newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia PM says party politics to stall ASEAN bid.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia PM says party politics to stall ASEAN bid.

text.p: Co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh on Monday said Cambodia's bid to join the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) would be stalled until dissident MPs in his royalist FUNCINPEC party were expelled.

Cambodia, Burma and Laos hope to join ASEAN in July, but officials of member states have voiced concern about political problems in Cambodia, where Ranariddh rules in an uneasy coalition with co-Premier Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party.

ASEAN leaders are due to meet in Kuala Lumpur on May 31 to decide whether to let the three nations join this year. The regional grouping comprises Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.

Feuding between the premiers, including Hun Sen's support for a challenge to Ranariddh's leadership of FUNCINPEC, has virtually paralysed government and forced the postponement of the regular parliamentary session.
Cambodia's national assembly must still pass 19 pieces of legislation for ASEAN membership, and lawmakers have said ASEAN wants the assembly to meet before the May 31 meeting.

But the prince, speaking at a school opening in the central province of Kompong Thom, said the FUNCINPEC steering committee wanted to expel eight dissident MPs and said the assembly could not legally adopt laws on ASEAN if they were allowed to vote.

"These eight MPs do not have the right to vote on the ASEAN law and this law will not be legally binding if these MPs can vote, so we have to solve this problem first," said Ranariddh, according to a tape of the speech made available to Reuters.
Political analysts said Ranariddh's warning indicated he was ready to use ASEAN membership as a bargaining chip in his destructive feud with Hun Sen.
Ranariddh also complained about a Phnom Penh Municipal Court ruling suspending the expulsions of some FUNCINPEC members.
Hun Sen has said he would not support the expulsions.

Ranariddh's threat to expel the eight, whose support Hun Sen is counting on to give his CPP a parliamentary majority, has stalled all parliamentary work, including meetings of the standing committee which would vote on expulsions.
The committee was expected to meet on Tuesday or Wednesday, MPs said.
Hun Sen and other officials have said parliament would not meet until head of state King Norodom Sihanouk returns home from China, where he has been receiving medical treatment for several weeks.
